doc.title: Dan Wall and Adam Nussbaum interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 19, 2001

title: Advice to young musicians and teaching at Oberlin
summary: Wall describes teaching pianists at Oberlin and says not to tell students they cannot make a living in music.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: Right. Well said. Let’s suppose you got asked to do a career day at a local high school and would you be encouraging to some aspiring musicians to try to make a living in this day and age? GW: Yeah well that’s an interesting comment because I was walking down the hall of Oberlin where I teach and I was listening to all of these people play this phenomenal, you know like I wish I could play the piano like this, it’s just ridiculous, and you have a violinist over here, and I was thinking what are they all going to do? Oh my gosh. But at the same time when I’m sitting in a room working with the pianist that I have, I’m not going to

give them that vibe and who knows what they can do until they get out there and try. I’m going to try to get them better. I’m going to sit there and play with them and work on their reaction time and work on their ears and try to play something back to them that they fall apart trying to play back to me so they’ll get better. So that they’ll go out there and see what they can do. Because that’s really what, you know I think that’s a big problem sometimes with say families where you have the family negative influence in saying, “Don’t go into music you’ll never make a living. Come into the family business. Be a doctor.” Well how do you know you can’t make a living? Don’t tell them that, tell them check it out but do it like a hundred percent. And then see what you can do. Or suppose they want to be an actor or a painter or whatever. And then later then it’s going to become pretty clear which way you’re going to have to go. Either it’s going to work or it’s not and you’re going to adjust to it.
